# Strut

Strut is an experimental memory-safe compiled language that emits native C++20. This website documents current development main at compiler checkpoint 378fce4. The latest tagged release is v0.0.3; pages explicitly label APIs that are newer than that release.

## Start here

- Documentation: https://strut-labs.github.io/docs.html
- Development versus release status: https://strut-labs.github.io/docs/status.html
- Getting started: https://strut-labs.github.io/getting-started.html
- Install the latest tagged release: https://strut-labs.github.io/install.html
- Machine-readable compiler API: run `strut api --json [query]`

## Current development APIs

- Bytes, Base64/Base64url, and crypto: https://strut-labs.github.io/docs/crypto.html
- Cancellation: https://strut-labs.github.io/docs/cancellation.html
- Outbound HTTP, including streaming: https://strut-labs.github.io/docs/http.html
- HTTP and HTTPS server: https://strut-labs.github.io/docs/http-server.html
- WebSocket server: https://strut-labs.github.io/docs/websockets.html
- Processes and lifecycle ownership: https://strut-labs.github.io/docs/processes.html
- Cross-platform pseudo-terminals, including Windows ConPTY: https://strut-labs.github.io/docs/pty.html
- Architecture and dependency boundaries: https://strut-labs.github.io/docs/architecture.html
- Security model and limits: https://strut-labs.github.io/docs/security.html
- API discovery schema: https://strut-labs.github.io/docs/api-schema.html

## Important limits

- Current-main APIs are not automatically available in the latest tagged v0.0.3 release.
- PTY execution is supported on Linux with glibc 2.34+, macOS, and Windows 10 1809 / Windows Server 2019 or newer through native ConPTY. Older Windows fails only `pty_spawn` with a deterministic checked error.
- ConPTY carries UTF-8/virtual-terminal traffic and its controls are Windows terminal/lifecycle approximations, not POSIX signals or arbitrary binary transparency.
- WebSockets are server-side only and have no compression/extensions.
- The HTTP client has no public client-certificate, explicit-proxy, or Unix-domain-socket option.
- The certified backend stack is not yet described as production-grade.
